facts.text: I've had several seizures, and other people saw them.
They are jerking movements of my left arm and leg.
I stay aware the whole time; I don't black out.
Each one lasts less than a minute.
They come every few minutes.
It began when I woke up with a headache, and then the seizures started.
I woke up with a headache.

facts.item: loss of bladder or bowel control during the seizures
facts.text: I didn't lose control of my bladder or bowels.
I didn't bite my tongue.
I wasn't confused afterwards.

facts.item: tingling and numbness on the left side
facts.text: I have tingling and numbness on my left side.
My vision hasn't changed.
My speech hasn't changed.
I haven't noticed any problems with my thinking or memory.
I have rheumatoid arthritis; I was told it's the seropositive type.
I take methotrexate for my arthritis.
I have high blood pressure.
I have small nodules in my lungs that have stayed stable.
I had a stroke before, in the right thalamus of the brain, and was treated with clot-busting medicine.
I had a single seizure during a previous hospital admission.
I didn't have any more seizures after that until now.
I've been taking levetiracetam since that seizure.
I take my levetiracetam as prescribed; I haven't missed doses.
My left leg is weak.

findings.name: observation of the episodes
findings.result: Repeated left-sided shaking involving the neck and extremities, with preserved consciousness.

findings.name: motor strength
findings.result: 3/5 strength in the left lower extremity.

findings.name: noncontrast head CT
findings.result: Sulcal effacement with isodense material suggestive of a leptomeningeal process.

findings.name: EEG
findings.result: Cortical hyperexcitability with focal seizure activity over the right frontocentral and parasagittal regions.

findings.name: MRI of the brain
findings.result: No acute infarction; focal right frontal pachymeningeal and leptomeningeal enhancement.

findings.name: viral serology
findings.result: Hepatitis B panel negative; hepatitis C panel negative; HIV negative.

findings.name: autoimmune serology
findings.result: Rheumatoid factor mildly elevated; anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody >250 U/mL; proteinase 3, myeloperoxidase, extractable nuclear antigens and anti-dsDNA negative; C3 and C4 negative.

findings.name: CSF analysis
findings.result: Normal cell counts, protein, and glucose.

findings.name: CSF cultures
findings.result: No growth on bacterial, fungal, and mycobacterial cultures.

findings.name: CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis

gold.reasoning: 1. Ischemic stroke was considered but excluded because “MRI of the brain ruled out ischemic stroke but indicated focal right frontal pachymeningeal and leptomeningeal enhancement with concerns for possible malignancy.” 2. Malignancy was considered due to the MRI findings but excluded by negative CSF cytology and flow cytometry — “...cytology, and flow cytometry, yielded negative results.” 3. Infectious meningitis was excluded because “CSF bacterial, fungal, and mycobacterial cultures also showed no growth.” 4. Tuberculous meningitis was less likely since on MRI the “basal cisterns are typically unaffected, in contrast with TB meningitis.” 5. Neurosarcoidosis was excluded because “angiotensin-converting enzyme ... were all negative.” 6. Neurosyphilis was excluded because “rapid plasma reagin ... [was] negative.” 7. Carcinomatous meningitis was excluded by the negative “cytology, and flow cytometry, yielded negative results.”

s006 contains the examination and, in a second sentence, the treatment (lorazepam, levetiracetam load).
Only 'hemodynamically stable' is given for vital signs.
notes: Index visit: the emergency presentation after multiple witnessed focal seizures (s001–s006); the imaging, EEG and laboratory workup (s007–s014) belong to the same admission.
s006 second sentence (lorazepam and a levetiracetam load controlled the seizures) is treatment during the workup and is not used.
x017 and x025 keep 'rheumatoid factor' in their aliases or names because the tests are named that way clinically.

Preserved awareness is a patient fact (f003) and stays in the observation finding (x003). The 3/5 left leg weakness is noticeable, so it is also a fact (f024); the pronator drift is an examiner finding only.
